abstract: In an effort to determine the impact of a delayed diagnosis in testicular cancer the records of 148 patients with a known interval of delay were reviewed. The over-all mean symptomatic interval of this population was 21.1 weeks and did not change significantly during an 18-year review period. An increased symptomatic interval correlated with an increased presenting stage of disease for nonseminoma and a delay of greater than 16 weeks strongly (p equals 0.002) lowered survival for these patients during the study interval. However, the symptomatic interval was not significantly associated with stage for seminoma patients nor did the symptomatic interval influence survival for these patients. Further analysis of the nonseminoma patients revealed that delay strongly affected survival (p equals 0.001) in the pre-cisplatin era (1970 to 1978) but it was less pronounced (p equals 0.262) in the cisplatin era (1979 to 1987). Despite an attenuation of the effect of delay in the current era of effective chemotherapy, deaths still occur due to delay in diagnosis and programs to lessen delay, such as testicular self-examination, and patient and physician education, are strongly encouraged.
abstract_ja: 精巣がん患者148例のうち、診断遅延期間が判明している症例の記録を検討した。全体の平均症状期間は21.1週で、18年間の検討期間中に有意な変化はなかった。症状期間が延長すると、非セミノーマ患者では病期がより進行し、遅延が16週を超えると生存率が強く低下した（p=0.002）。一方、セミノーマ患者では症状期間と病期に有意な関連はなく、生存にも影響しなかった。非セミノーマ患者をさらに解析すると、遅延はシスプラチン導入前の時代（1970〜1978年）には生存に強く影響していた（p=0.001）が、シスプラチン時代（1979〜1987年）では影響がやや弱まっていた（p=0.262）。有効な化学療法が行われる現在でも、影響は弱まっているものの、診断遅延による死亡は依然として生じている。精巣自己検診や患者・医師への啓発などにより遅延を減らす取り組みが強く推奨される。
